newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close at new high after bank frenzy.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close at new high after bank frenzy.

text.p: Swedish shares closed at a new record on Tuesday but off the day's highs after a hectic day of trade amid a frenzy of bank activity and a construction company merger.
The Stockholm general index rose 0.25 percent to 2,649.34 but was up to 0.50 percent higher around midday.
A hefty 5.82 billion crowns worth of shares changed hands.
The main focus was the foreshadowed merger of Swedbank and Foreningsbanken with details released.
"(The merger) is positive for the market," said analyst Peter Thorn from Paribas.
The banking sector jumped 5.30 percent as Swedbank shares soared 20 crowns to 139.5 crowns when trading resumed. Foreningsbanken closed 4.70 crowns higher at 43.20 crowns.
The annual earnings of other banks released on Tuesday were generally better than expected and well received by the market.
Nordbanken closed 20 crowns higher at 255 crowns after posting a 10 percent rise in operating profit. The bank said the doors were still open to continue talks for a future possible partner.
Handelsbanken announced a 33 percent jump in profits. It rose 6.5 to 207.5 crowns.
The construction sector was another of the day's winners rising 3.54 percent after NCC and Siab announced a merger.
NCC shares closed 3.50 higher at 89.50 crowns and Siab jumped 11 to 51 crowns.
Blue chip Ericsson slumped in later trade, losing four crowns to 246.
"On GSM we are expecting a price lowering of 20-25 percent," Ericsson's marketing head for mobile phones told Reuters.
The share was also hit by jitters in Finish rival Nokia after its trading recommendation was downgraded by NatWest.
Swedish bus and truck maker Scania lost five crowns to 191 after posting a 44 percent slump in 1996 profits after financial items to 2.71 billion crowns.
The forestry sector lost some of its recent gains, slipping 1.85 percent.
Forestry company MoDo, due to release its 1996 earnings on Wednesday, closed 5.5 crowns lower at 228 crowns.
